summary: IDS feed c028_crc_span is severely degraded: 63.33% SPAN loss from oversubscription (2.73 Gbps into 1 Gbps) plus CRC errors on ingress. IDS is blind to majority of traffic and receives corrupted frames, breaking detection.

findings.root_cause: VF-1 port 3 (input) is receiving damaged frames at 0.1394% (14,940 CRC/alignment errors, threshold 0.001%) indicating a Layer-1 fault - faulty cable, optic, or duplex mismatch on the link into the packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires complete, correct payload for signature and anomaly detection. Corrupted frames fail parsing/reassembly and cause missed detections and false negatives; IDS wastes cycles on unusable packets.

recommended_fix.why: Physical layer must be clean before any broker fix; replace cable/optic, verify duplex/speed negotiation, and clear counters to confirm zero CRC/alignment errors.

findings.root_cause: CORE-SW-01 SPAN is fundamentally oversubscribed: Gi1/0/1 mirrors 29,217,840 packets (2.73 Gbps) into Gi1/0/48 SPAN destination limited to 1 Gbps. Destination discarded 18,503,520 packets (63.33% loss) at 100% average load, bursts higher. SPAN destination cannot buffer or backpressure.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS with 1 Gbps port and needs_both_directions=true / needs_full_payload=true loses 63% of packets. Creates massive blind spot - IDS misses attacks, cannot reconstruct flows, and state tables are incomplete. Loss is random, so detection coverage is non-deterministic.

recommended_fix.why: Replace lossy SPAN with passive TAP for lossless capture, then handle 2.73Gbps > 1Gbps mismatch via packet broker: filter to IDS-relevant traffic, or load_balance across multiple 1G IDS sensors, or upgrade IDS to 10G. TAP eliminates SPAN scheduler drops and preserves both directions.
